Finding: Forecast differs from actual service throughput
Evidence: Maximum-level 22-guest tests: forecast exceeds recorded earned/min by 12.45–13.07%; base by 1.96–2.29%. Inactive and offline income use this forecast.
Recommended change: Calibrate the estimator against the same service phases, traversal and tips, or explicitly define passive production as a separate rate.
Acceptance criterion: At base/mid/max levels and all five districts, published rate agrees with long-window selected-outlet production within an agreed tolerance (proposed ±5%).

Finding: PLAY stays selected on every screen
Evidence: Bottom buttons are colored once in BuildCanvas; Navigate rebuilds body but never updates those colors. Fresh map screenshot shows PLAY highlighted.
Recommended change: Track navigation buttons and update selected state on every transition.
Acceptance criterion: Map/Team/Play/Lab/Goals each show exactly one correct active tab.

Finding: Choose and validate the intended progression horizon
Evidence: New matched max-all model: family 5.43h versus Traffic Flow Current 422.76h / New 356.38h. All use 10,800 upgrades under the same spending policy. These are conditional forecasts, not measured duration.
Recommended change: Retain the deliberate free-family direction, decide the desired content horizon and validate milestones in gameplay. Keep historical v0.2.0 parity percentages out of current release claims.
Acceptance criterion: Report open-all, max-all, team/research and repeat-star milestones separately, with consistent endpoints and observed checkpoints.

Evidence: Current map capture: the first node wraps to three description lines and the last line extends below its card. Larger-text layouts increase risk.
Recommended change: Use content-driven row height or a fixed two-line description; test wrapping at supported sizes.
Acceptance criterion: No clipping, overlap or hidden cost at portrait aspect ratios and larger text.

Finding: No Android runtime or child usability evidence
Evidence: No device attached. Build manifest is verified, but source/Editor and 15s recording cannot establish phone input, thermal stability or understanding.
Recommended change: Run clean install, 30-minute device sessions and first-session usability with a ten-year-old.
Acceptance criterion: Real touch, pause/resume, recovery, safe areas and sustained performance pass on named Android 11+ midrange devices.

Finding: Dining teammate speed is unused in family service
Evidence: Independent Mythic Dining teammate test: speed vector +240%, eating duration remains 3.8s; Dining pay increases 6→9. Affinity vector is not consumed by the family service equations.
Recommended change: Either apply meaningful role/affinity effects or remove unsupported stats/data; show assignment and before/after impact.
Acceptance criterion: Each displayed teammate effect changes an observable or economic outcome; role/affinity usefulness is tested.

Finding: Restaurant world and food are too small
Evidence: Fresh portrait shots devote much of the upper screen to header/outlet/guide; food is a small fraction of a character. Bright floor/counters/chairs merge.
Recommended change: Compact header and guide; frame the service area more closely; establish material/value separation and food focal lighting.
Acceptance criterion: A viewer can identify the current dish, where to order and which table is free at normal phone size.

Finding: Completion and upgrades lack persistent visual payoff
Evidence: Service result is a short toast plus sound; upgrades mostly change numbers/timers, with no equipment evolution. Traffic Flow gives a structured departure summary.
Recommended change: Add a brief non-blocking service summary, coin flight, ticket reveal, upgrade pulse and milestone equipment changes.
Acceptance criterion: Six-guest onboarding completion communicates meals, earned coins and ticket clearly; feedback respects reduced motion.

Finding: District icons do not identify individual outlets
Evidence: Street nodes share a burger icon, including Taco Terrace and Noodle Nook. The path is a scrolling connected list rather than a spatial restaurant world.
Recommended change: Keep district emblems but add signature-food outlet icons, district landmarks and a clear next objective.
Acceptance criterion: Every outlet icon matches its cuisine; current/next/locked nodes and requirements are visually distinct.

Finding: One served food prefab per outlet; food removal is renderer-based
Evidence: Every NewDish instantiates the same outlet food. Portion animation hides sorted renderers; it is not bite-shape animation or a menu-order system.
Recommended change: Add two or three recognizable dish/order variants with explicit edible portions and matching hand/utensil actions.
Acceptance criterion: Each visible menu item has an appropriate dish; plate remains stable while food disappears logically.

Finding: Five districts share one service topology
Evidence: Family rules bypass original vehicle capacity/body/segment/timing differences. All districts reuse one order counter, two cook slots and twelve chairs.
Recommended change: Introduce modest district-specific station layouts/behaviors while keeping the free economy understandable; recalibrate every change.
Acceptance criterion: New district introduces a clearly visible difference beyond palette/menu/income scale.

Finding: Unclaimed rewards can accumulate above one-day cap
Evidence: Two isolated 24h Resume calls before a claim accumulate 367,810.79 from a 127.71/min forecast; one-day value is 183,905.39. Original Traffic Flow carries credited time and caps the pending bucket.
Recommended change: Decide whether cap is per absence or total pending; make wording and tests match. Do not call the current behavior exact reference parity.
Acceptance criterion: Boundary tests cover >300s, 24h, repeated unclaimed returns and duplicate claims; documented behavior matches UI.

Finding: Menu rebuilding and mixed labels add cognitive load
Evidence: GOALS opens rewards before the goal list; descriptions use research/teammate abstractions; world motion reduction and larger text exist but need device validation.
Recommended change: Make Goals open goals directly; show useful upgrade outcomes; provide icon+text and test all large-text pages.
Acceptance criterion: An unaided new player can find the next action and explain its purpose.

Evidence: Runtime wires music, coin, tap and upgrade clips; no separate pickup/chop/grill/sit/bite/plate-return hooks are visible in the service code. Concept soundtrack event lists are not proof of runtime wiring.
Recommended change: Add restrained event-driven kitchen and dining sounds with a mixer/voice budget and sensible cooldowns.
Acceptance criterion: Sounds follow actual service events, remain clear under load, and honor SFX/music switches.

Finding: Repeatability is mostly the same loop with higher values
Evidence: Stars retain upgrades and can repeat every five services after maxing; goals repeat in books; finite 40-outlet art/content remains. There is no verified endless stream of new mechanics.
Recommended change: Add earned cosmetic/recipe goals and optional challenges that create variety without coercive timers or payments.
Acceptance criterion: Post-map-clear sessions offer meaningful choices; content and expected repetition are honestly described.

Finding: Testing APK is not a store-ready release
Evidence: Current APK is non-debuggable ARM64, but prior signature report says Android debug certificate; no store AAB/release validation shown.
Recommended change: Prepare publisher signing, AAB, diagnostics, icon/listing and required store declarations after gameplay acceptance.
Acceptance criterion: Release artifact, device matrix and store setup verified separately from Editor/build checks.
